subject: NeonCloud: SKU wedging & regional safety-margin proposal for tri-geo reserved pool
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amira Qureshi <amira@neoncloud.com>, contracts@neoncloud.com
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: NeonCloud: SKU wedging & regional safety-margin proposal for tri-geo reserved pool

Team—

NeonCloud (DEAL-8472) is asking for a dedicated-reserved footprint recommendation that covers APAC primary (Jakarta + Singapore edge), EU fallback, and US failover. The ask includes:

- Sustained baseline: 4M tokens/day (profile attached) with spikes up to 2.5x for product launches.
- Hard SLO: p95 latency < 250ms for chat generation in APAC.
- Data residency: Singapore for APAC workloads (Amira copied).

I want a concise "wedge" plan: a small reserved buffer across regions (safety wedge) plus a deal-anchored sustained allocation. Please propose:

1) Recommended device mix (H100 / A100 equivalence) and count per region for baseline + 30% wedge.
2) Burst/backstop sizing (short-term extra nodes) and how many tokens/sec they buy us.
3) Operational caveats (quantization, caching, model variants) and cost tradeoffs.
4) Any redlines that should go into the SOW (e.g., failover times, cross-region egress caps).

Attachments: NeonCloud-traffic-profiles-20260916.csv (traffic percentiles and token-length distribution).

Can I get a recommendation by EOD PST today so I can include it in the draft SOW?

Thanks,
David
David Kim
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amira Qureshi <amira@neoncloud.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 15:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: NeonCloud: SKU wedging & regional safety-margin proposal for tri-geo reserved pool

Quick sizing note (high-level):

Summary recommendation (baseline + 30% wedge):
- APAC (primary; Singapore residency + Jakarta edge): 6x H100-equivalent serving nodes (sustained), +2x H100-equivalent burst nodes.
- EU (fallback): 3x A100-equivalent serving nodes (sustained), +1x A100-equivalent burst node.
- US (failover): 2x A100-equivalent serving nodes (warm standby).

Rationale / assumptions:
- Baseline 4M tokens/day -> ~46 tokens/sec sustained (24/7) but traffic is spiky; 95th percentile spikes equate to ~115 tokens/sec. We size for sustained plus a 30% wedge to preserve p95 SLOs.
- H100-equivalent nodes used in APAC because of superior perf for long-context chat (model: LlamaX-70B-ILQL variant). EU/US can use cheaper A100-equivalent nodes for fallback.

Burst/backstop model:
- 2x H100 burst nodes in APAC provide ~200 tokens/sec headroom for 10–20 minute spikes; automated routing + graceful degradation to smaller context models on overflow.
- Cross-region fallback: traffic routed to EU within 90s if APAC bursts exceed threshold; contracts should specify max cross-region egress per month to control costs.

Operational notes (things to include in SOW):
- Failover target: route shift to EU in <= 90s on sustained overload; full failover to US in <= 5 minutes for catastrophic APAC outage.
- Cache warmup: initial cold-starts for KV-cache will affect few minutes after deploy; recommend a 72-hour ramp window for new deployments.
- Quantization profile: recommend 4-bit hybrid for APAC serving to save ~28% cost while preserving quality for NeonCloud's RL-finetuned models; log a quality regression threshold in the SLOs.
- Autoscaling policy: preserve at least 1 reserved node per region (cannot scale below).

Costs: rough delta vs baseline (monthly):
- APAC: +$98k/mo (6 H100 eq. + wedge + 2 burst nodes amortized)
- EU: +$34k/mo
- US: +$18k/mo
(These are order-of-magnitude; procurement will provide firm pricing.)

Attachments: sku-wedge-calcs-20260917.xlsx — contains token-to-GPU mappings, expected p95 latencies per node type, and cost deltas.

Next steps:
- If team agrees, I can fold these numbers into an SOW appendix and add failover language for cross-region egress caps.

-karthik

From: Amira Qureshi <amira@neoncloud.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@neoncloud.com
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 02:10:00 +0800
Subject: Re: NeonCloud: SKU wedging & regional safety-margin proposal for tri-geo reserved pool

Thanks David + Karthik — this looks promising. A few clarifications from our side before we proceed to SOW: 

- Singapore data residency is a hard requirement for APAC workloads; can you confirm the APAC "6x H100-equivalent" nodes can be provisioned in Singapore region (not just Jakarta)?
- We would prefer a slightly larger APAC burst buffer during launch weeks (up to +50% for two-week windows). Can that be modeled as a short-term addendum to the reserved pool (prepaid bursts)?
- On failover timings: 90s to EU is acceptable, but we need a guaranteed SLO for cross-region routing latency (p50/p95 on added hop). Can Redwood provide observed numbers from similar customers?

Also flagged by Legal: include explicit limits for cross-region data transfer in the SOW appendix and a mechanism for NeonCloud to request a one-time uplift of the wedge during major campaigns (pricing and notice period required).

Appreciate the fast turnaround — happy to hop on a 30m call Monday (SGT) to finalize.

Cheers,
Amira Qureshi
Head of Platform Operations, NeonCloud

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Amira Qureshi <amira@neoncloud.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@ben.redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@neoncloud.com
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NeonCloud: SKU wedging & regional safety-margin proposal for tri-geo reserved pool

Amira — thanks for the quick read and the asks. Confirmations & next steps below: 

1) Singapore residency: procurement ops can provision the 6x H100-equivalent nodes in Singapore; Jakarta will be used as an edge POP for low-latency egress where required. I'll add explicit wording in the SOW that APAC reserved nodes are Singapore-hosted.

2) Launch burst: we can model a prepaid burst addendum for up to +50% capacity for 14-day windows with a 7-day notice and a capped uplift fee. I'll include a pricing bracket in the SOW appendix.

3) Cross-region routing metrics: we have anonymized p50/p95 traces from prior customers — I'll attach a short anonymized latency report and propose p50=40ms (intra-APAC edge), p95=120–200ms on cross-region hops (depends on destination). I'll drop the internal trace link into the HubSpot record.

Action items: 
- Karthik: finalize the SKU appendix and include the quantization/regression clause — due COB Tue.
- Ben: coordinate with procurement to get Singapore node cost estimate and confirm H100 availability for requested time window — due Wed.
- Vanessa: put together SOW draft (I attached SOW-draft-NeonCloud-8472-v1.pdf) and add the cross-region egress clause + prepaid-burst language.
- Soojin: prepare the anonymized latency report for NeonCloud and upload to the shared drive.

I'll schedule a 30m call for Mon 21 Sep 09:00 SGT / Sun 20 Sep 20:00 PDT and send an invite.

Thanks all — David

Attachments: SOW-draft-NeonCloud-8472-v1.pdf
